concepts.why: The presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass involving the temporal bone, along with thickening of the inner table, supports the diagnosis of an osteoma.

The symptoms of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area, along with the presence of fluid in the right mastoid air cells and mucosal thickening in the right ethmoid air cells, suggest a diagnosis of mastoiditis.
The presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass with mild patchy internal enhancement supports the diagnosis of an osteoblastoma.
The symptoms of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area, along with the presence of a hyperostotic lesion and thickening of the inner table, suggest a diagnosis of chronic osteomyelitis.
The presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass involving the temporal bone could be associated with Gardner syndrome, although other findings are not typical for this condition.

The symptoms of pain and swelling in the right mastoid area, along with the presence of a hyperostotic lesion and fluid in the right mastoid air cells, could suggest a diagnosis of eosinophilic granuloma.
The presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass with mild patchy internal enhancement could be consistent with fibrous dysplasia.

Although less likely, the presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass involving the temporal bone could be associated with osteosarcoma, but other findings do not strongly support this diagnosis.

The presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass involving the temporal bone could be associated with a chondroma, although this is less likely given the specific characteristics of the mass.

The presence of a hyperostotic lesion and a densely calcified mass involving the temporal bone could be associated with an osteochondroma, although other findings do not strongly support this diagnosis.
It explains the hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium without intracranial extension or adjacent soft-tissue mass.
